A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEMA study. All 37 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SEMA experiments on AdvBench and HarmBench, including baseline comparisons, transfer results, ablations, scalability tests, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, even though no new results are added.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same open-loop generation procedure, prefilling self-tuning, GRPO objective, and intent-drift-aware reward. The evaluation-judge specification changes separately from the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AdvBench and HarmBench coverage and retain the same generalization and transfer scenarios. Appendix evaluations involving GPT-4o, GPT-oss-20B, and Qwen3 Guard already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including ActorAttack, X-Teaming, SFT/DPO, Augmentation in scalability tests, and X-Teaming-IS in Table 11.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1.3 changes the stated LLM Classifier backend from GPT-4.1-mini to GPT-4o-mini, retaining its prompt and temperature. Section 4.2 changes the first listed scalability budget from N=1 to N=5. These are reported setting revisions; unchanged tables and curves do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The reward, prefilling, turn-count, model, and training-evaluator ablations are retained, as are generalization tests, case studies, X-Teaming re-evaluation, cost analysis, and attack-diversity analysis. Expanded discussion adds no analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, Figure 7 retains its uncertainty displays, and Appendix C.1.4 retains the repeated-evaluation description. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported scores, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. Examples include Table 2's 80.1% mean AdvBench ASR@1 and Appendix D.3's 15.1% reversal of initially successful X-Teaming judgments. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and objectives in Section 3 and metric definitions in Appendix C.1.4, including Equations 1–13, are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-stage open-loop learning, independence from external strategy corpora, and leading success, transferability, and scalability. Adding 'prior' before 'SOTA' does not change the comparison's meaning.

C2.justification: The new Ethics Statement explicitly discusses dual-use risks, planned responsible-use guidance, and the absence of human subjects, personal data, or real targets. These add use and study-scope qualifications. Existing scientific interpretations and Appendix E's technical limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The code repository pointer changes from fmmarkmq/SEMA to microsoft/SEMA. A new Reproducibility Statement directs readers to existing appendix settings and templates; it does not supply new training or hardware details. The evaluation-judge designation is also revised in Appendix C.1.3.

R1.justification: The cited works, six-axis comparisons in Tables 1 and 10, and positioning against prior attacks remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 expands an existing criticism of internal-judge evaluation without introducing a new research-positioning argument.

P1.justification: v2 adds Ethics and Reproducibility Statements after the conclusion and makes localized wording edits to dataset descriptions, generalization discussion, and baseline-evaluation explanations. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The new statements fill previously blank space on page 10, and references begin there instead of page 11. Local text expansion shifts Tables 11 and 12 downward on page 35. Figures and tables retain their designs and contents.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves documentation and navigation through its reproducibility roadmap, explicit ethical scope, and clearer baseline-evaluation explanation. The scientific method, evidence, and technical limitations remain unchanged. The judge-name revision is not explained as either a correction or a rerun, so it provides no basis for claiming stronger empirical support.
